_note: Display metadata for the MCP servers the Woven harness wires into spawned CLI subprocesses (claude via --mcp-config, codex via -c mcp_servers overrides, opencode via the managed OPENCODE_CONFIG). Sibling of .claude/mcp-config.json (the runtime config). Surfaced under landing → System → MCP. Edit this file to add new servers (also add the runtime entry to mcp-config.json - they're intentionally kept separate so mcp-config.json stays a strict Claude-Code --mcp-config payload).

servers.label: Chrome DevTools
servers.purpose: Drive a real browser via the DevTools Protocol. Launches its own headless, isolated Chrome - zero setup, nothing to start, no user profile touched.
servers.whenToUse: Escalation path. The agent reaches for it only when built-in WebFetch returns 401 / 403 / a login wall, or when a page is JS-rendered and WebFetch's HTML comes back empty - and for Testing-node runs that click through a live prototype.
requires: Node.js / npx available on PATH (so the daemon can spawn the server)
servers.firstCallNote: First call cold-resolves the npm package and boots a Chromium - allow it a beat. No flags or relaunches needed from the user.

servers.label: Figma
servers.purpose: Read and generate Figma designs through Figma's official hosted MCP. Same `mcp-remote` proxy pattern as Claude Desktop's connector flow.
servers.whenToUse: When the user mentions Figma, pastes a figma.com URL, or asks to read / generate a design from Figma source.
requires: A Figma account (free tier is fine - only files you own or are shared into are reachable)
servers.firstCallNote: First call opens an OAuth flow in your default browser. Approve once; the token persists in mcp-remote's local cache so subsequent runs are silent.
